---
title: BEDbase
description: BEDbase's catalog of BED files and bedsets as resource tables, with the region data itself referenced, not copied.
---

[BEDbase](https://bedbase.org) catalogs hundreds of thousands of BED files,
mostly GEO and ENCODE peak and region calls processed through its bedboss
pipeline, grouped into bedsets. bioc-on-ice carries the catalog, not the
intervals: the `resource` tables say what each file is, which genome it is
on and where it came from, and the bytes stay at BEDbase.

The release lands BEDbase's own monthly Parquet snapshot (the index at
`api.bedbase.org/v1/exports`), never a crawl of the API: a crawl of
`/bed/list` in September 2026 took the service down for an hour and a half.
The version is the snapshot's date.

## Licence and citation

BEDbase states no site-wide data licence. Each record carries a
[DUO](https://github.com/EBISPOT/DUO) code, and every record of the 2026-09-01
snapshot is `DUO:0000042`, general research use. Cite BEDbase as its site
asks.

## Join keys

- `resource.bedbase__bedfile.resource_id` and `resource.bedbase__bedset.resource_id` are the BEDbase ids.
- Membership is in `resource.resource_relationship` as `member_of_bedset` rows, and GEO and ENCODE origins as `encode:ENCSR…` / `encode:ENCFF…` targets that join `resource.encode__*.resource_id` with `=`.
- Genomes are keyed on `genome_digest`, never `genome_alias`: the alias is free text and one Arabidopsis record carries `hg18`.
- `taxon_id` is a `TRY_CAST` of the species field, which is occasionally a comma-separated pair; it is NULL on those rows.

## Good to know

- Per-file size, checksum, URIs and bedstat statistics are not in the snapshot ([#115](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice/issues/115)).
- The raw column names predate the snapshot (`annotation_*`, from the old listing API) and are kept.
- Only `ENCSR` targets that are ENCODE *experiments* resolve in `resource.encode__experiment`; most name ENCODE Annotation datasets, which are not landed.
